quickstart.title: Quick Start
quickstart.subtitle: From zero to your first successful API call in about 3 minutes.

step1.title: Get your API key
step1.desc: After signing up, an initial token is automatically generated. Go to Console → Token Management to copy it.
step1.security: Never expose your API key in frontend code, public repositories, or client apps. Always read it from server-side environment variables.

step2.title: Choose a model
step2.desc: We recommend deepseek-v4-flash for your first call — it's fast, affordable, and great for testing.
step2.dynamicFallback: Showing the verified default model while the live catalog loads.

step3.title: Choose your calling method
step3.desc: Vancine is OpenAI-compatible. You can call it directly via HTTP or use the official OpenAI SDK.
step3.httpDesc: Use curl, fetch, or any HTTP client to call the REST API directly.
step3.sdkDesc: Drop-in replacement: just change base_url and api_key in your existing OpenAI SDK code.

step4.title: Make your first call
step4.desc: Copy the code below, replace sk-your-api-key with your real key, and run it.

infoTable.title: Essential information
infoTable.tip: GET /v1/models requires an API key and lists models available to the current token. GET /api/pricing is public and exposes endpoint support plus pricing metadata.

exploreMore.title: Explore more
exploreMore.desc: Now that you're up and running, check out what else Vancine can do:

recommendedModels.dynamicHelp: The list reflects the live catalog. When the live catalog is unavailable, the page falls back to a verified set of currently online models.

migrate.title: Migrate from OpenAI
migrate.hook: Vancine is fully compatible with the OpenAI API. Existing code usually only needs two changes — base_url and api_key — while everything else (SDK, endpoints, response structure, streaming, function calling) stays the same.

twoChanges.title: Only 2 changes needed
twoChanges.desc: Take your existing OpenAI code, change the base URL and API key, and it works.

fullExamples.title: Full examples
fullExamples.desc: Complete working examples in Python, Node.js, and cURL.

whatStaysSame.title: What stays the same
whatStaysSame.desc: Everything else in your codebase works without modification:

sameItems.sdk: Same openai Python / Node.js SDK — no new dependency
sameItems.functionCalling: Function calling / tool use is supported

comparison.title: Migration comparison
comparison.apiKeyNote: Use your Vancine token from Console → Tokens

nextSteps.title: Next steps
nextSteps.desc: Ready to go deeper? Check out these pages:

chat.title: Chat Completions
chat.desc: Send an OpenAI-compatible messages array to a language model and receive a synchronous JSON response.
chat.reasoningCallout: Reasoning models may leave `content` empty while `reasoning_content` is populated; `finish_reason: length` often means the token budget was spent on reasoning, not that the API failed. The Models page lists which text models are reasoning-capable.

params.model: Model name. Use any currently online text model; see the Models page for the live list.
params.maxTokens: Maximum generated tokens; use a larger value for reasoning models

image.title: Image Generation
image.desc: Generate images from text prompts. The response is synchronous JSON with temporary image URLs in the data array.
image.sizeWarning: Doubao-Seedream-5.0-lite requires at least 3,686,400 pixels. 1024x1024 returns “image size must be at least 3686400 pixels”; use 2048x2048. Doubao-Seedream-5.0-pro has no such limit: minimum 921,600 pixels (1024x1024 works), but it only supports single-image generation (no image groups). Both support 1K/2K resolution tiers (lite also supports 3K/4K); the model decides the final size.

params.size: Size in WIDTHxHEIGHT format (see size table below)
params.response_format: Return format: url (default, temporary link valid for 24 hours) or b64_json
params.output_format: Output format: png or jpeg (default jpeg). Only Seedream 5.0 pro/lite support this
params.image: Reference image URL or Base64 for image-to-image / multi-image fusion (5.0 pro: max 10, lite: max 14)
params.watermark: Whether to add watermark. Seedream defaults to false

image.advancedParamsCallout: Advanced Seedream parameters such as sequential_image_generation (image groups) and optimize_prompt_options (prompt optimization) require PassThrough to be enabled on the channel. They are not forwarded by default.
image.intro: Image generation is synchronous: POST a request to /v1/images/generations and the response carries the image URL (or base64) in the data array. The models below are the ones the platform currently advertises; each has a dedicated page documenting the exact request schema.
image.modelsIntro: Each model below is in the live pricing catalog. Each has a dedicated page documenting the exact request schema.
image.commonParamsDesc: These fields apply to every currently online image model. Each model page documents its own additional parameters (size tiers, n range, reference limits, advanced features).
image.examplesIntro: The example below uses a currently online image model and sends the minimum legal request (model + prompt + n + size). Each model page documents a model-specific example with the exact request body.

commonParams.model: Model name. The page lists every currently online image model.
commonParams.prompt: Text prompt. No fixed character cap beyond the gateway body-size limit; per-model notes live on the model page.
commonParams.n: Image count. The legal range is per-model (Qwen 3.x: 1–6; Wan 2.7 Pro: 1–4; Seedream 5.0 pro/lite: always 1). See the model page for the exact range.
commonParams.size: Image size. Each model exposes its own size tiers; the model page lists every legal value, the default, and the per-tier constraints.
commonParams.responseFormat: Return format: `url` (default, temporary link valid 24h) or `b64_json`. All online models accept this.
commonParams.watermark: Whether to embed a watermark. Default is false for every online model; the exact default is documented per model.
commonParams.image: Reference image (URL or Base64) for image-to-image / multi-image fusion. The maximum reference count, accepted MIME types, and per-image size cap are per-model; see the model page.

image.advancedParamsNote: Each model page documents its own advanced parameters. Image models share these common fields; the model page is the source of truth for size tiers, n range, and reference limits.

video.title: Video Generation
video.desc: Video generation is asynchronous. Save the top-level id from the submission response, then poll GET /v1/video/generations/{id}.

params.image: Single reference image URL or Base64 (image-to-video)
params.images: Array of reference image URLs (multi-image input)

video.metadataCallout: There is no "shared metadata block" — the legal fields inside `metadata` are model-specific. The dedicated model page lists every legal key and value for that model.

status.success: Done (status: SUCCESS). Read `data.result_url` for the result video URL.
status.submitQueued: The submit receipt reports status queued (lowercase). The task has been accepted and is not yet running.
status.notStart: The task has not started (status: NOT_START).
status.submitted: The task has been submitted (status: SUBMITTED).

video.intro: Video generation is an async task workflow: submit a request, save the task id, and poll the same path until the status reaches a terminal value, then read the result URL or the failure reason. Each currently online model has a dedicated page documenting its exact wire contract — durations, resolutions, reference-image rules, and the precise JSON shape.
video.modelsIntro: Each model below is in the live pricing catalog. The exact wire contract (durations, resolutions, reference-image slots) lives on the per-model detail page.
video.modelsDiffer: Video models do not share a single parameter schema. The exact wire contract (top-level `duration` vs STRING `seconds`, `size` vs `metadata.resolution`, `metadata.input.media` vs `metadata.content` for reference images) is documented per model on the model page.
video.examplesIntro: The example below sends the minimum legal request (model + prompt) and then polls the same path until the status is one of the terminal values. Each model page documents a model-specific example with the exact wire contract (duration vs seconds, size vs metadata.resolution, metadata.content vs metadata.input.media).
video.commonParamsDesc: These fields are common to every video model. The model-specific fields (duration vs seconds, size vs metadata.resolution, reference-image slot) are documented on the model page.

commonParams.model: Video model name. Each online model has a dedicated page listing the exact wire contract.
commonParams.prompt: Text prompt. Trimmed before submit; empty is rejected client-side.

auth.desc: All /v1 requests require an API key in the Authorization header.

auth.exampleModel: Any currently online text model works. See the Models page for the live list.

pi.title: Pi Coding Agent
pi.desc: Install the Vancine Pi Provider from npm, then sign in with your own Vancine API Key and pick a model.

common.baseUrlDesc: Use this exact Base URL for every OpenAI-compatible request. Do not add extra path segments.
common.configNote: The example only contains placeholder credentials. Replace sk-your-api-key with your own Vancine API key locally; never commit it.
common.modelsDesc: Use any Vancine text (chat) model. Live model capabilities, context limits and prices are maintained on the Models and Pricing pages, not on this page.

baseUrl.symptom: 404, CORS or connection errors; requests hit another host.
baseUrl.fix: Set the Base URL exactly to {{baseUrl}} with no extra path segments.

apiKey.fix: Copy the full Vancine API key without spaces. If it was rotated or deleted, create a new one in your key management.

model.symptom: model not found / model does not exist.
model.fix: Use an exact model ID from the Vancine model list. Model IDs are case-sensitive. The live Models page is the source of truth; copy the id verbatim.

protocol.fix: Check the protocol the tool expects: most OpenAI-compatible tools use Chat Completions (/v1/chat/completions); Codex-style Responses tools need /v1/responses. Choose the matching option in {{tool}}.

common.notOfficial: Vancine is an independent OpenAI-compatible API service. It is not an official provider, partner or built-in integration of {{tool}}.
common.statusCallout: The OpenAI-compatible setup for this tool is ready. Follow this guide to connect it to Vancine.

opencode.valueProp: OpenCode loads Vancine from the Models.dev provider catalog; the dynamic Models page is the source of truth for available model ids.
opencode.noJsonNote: Basic setup does not require creating or editing opencode.json.
opencode.step2: Create a Vancine account and an API Key if you do not have them yet.
opencode.step5: Paste your own Vancine API Key.
opencode.step7: Choose vancine/{{modelId}}, or another model under the vancine Provider, then send a prompt.

opencode.notOfficial: Vancine is an independent OpenAI-compatible API service listed in the Models.dev catalog used by OpenCode. This catalog listing does not imply an official partnership or endorsement by OpenCode.

model.fix: Use the exact model ID from the Vancine live catalog. Model IDs are case-sensitive. The Models page is the source of truth.

opencode.benchmarkNote: The linked 8-model benchmark was run in the Pi coding agent, not in OpenCode: it shows these models complete real coding-agent tasks through Vancine. OpenCode connectivity itself is covered by the v1.18.3 live check described on this page, and no other OpenCode version has been verified.
opencode.catalogProof: Available in OpenCode through the Models.dev provider catalog
opencode.catalogNote: OpenCode loads its provider catalog from Models.dev. Vancine is listed there as an OpenAI-compatible Provider. You still use your own Vancine API Key.

verifyKey.q: How do I verify an API key?
verifyKey.a: Call GET {{baseUrl}}/models. HTTP 200 with a model list means the key is valid and has access in the current group.

seedreamSize.q: Why does Seedream reject my image size?
seedreamSize.a: Doubao-Seedream-5.0-lite requires at least 3,686,400 pixels (use 2048x2048). Doubao-Seedream-5.0-pro has no such limit: minimum 921,600 pixels (1024x1024 works). Set size for the model you use, or pass a 1K/2K tier and let the model decide.

common.notFoundDesc: The documentation page you are looking for does not exist.
common.pageNotReady: This page is not ready yet. Check back soon!

modelDetail.contractMissing: No verified contract is published for this model yet. The page intentionally shows no fabricated parameters.

image.refs: Reference images: up to {{max}} per request. Accepted MIME types: {{mimes}}.

meta.description: {{summary}} Exact request schema, supported parameters, and verified examples for the Vancine API.
meta.title: {{modelId}} API reference | Vancine

modelDetail.pricingDesc: Pricing is dynamic and listed on the live Pricing page; availability and tier prices are not duplicated here.
modelDetail.verified: Verified on {{date}} against {{source}}. The request schema is the production contract; a wire change upstream will surface here.

video.bodyLimit: Request body budget: {{mb}} MB. The studio enforces this limit before submit; going over is rejected client-side.
video.paramDuration: Top-level integer in [{{min}}, {{max}}]. The upstream rejects durations outside this range.
video.paramModel: Must be exactly "{{modelId}}". Case-sensitive; the server rejects other strings.
video.paramPrompt: Free-form text prompt. Trimmed before submit; empty is rejected client-side.
video.paramRefs: Up to {{max}} reference image items, each { "type": "image_url", "role": "reference_image", "image_url": { "url": "..." } }. Allowed MIME: jpeg, png, webp.
video.paramResolution: One of {{list}}. Wan3 / MiniMax-H3 / Seedance each spell this slightly differently; the doc above shows the exact string for this model.
video.paramSecondsString: Top-level STRING in [{{min}}, {{max}}] (NOT a JSON number — Go types it as a string).
video.paramSizeWan3: Top-level resolution (Wan3 contract). One of {{list}}. Equivalent to setting metadata.resolution; the studio uses the top-level slot.
video.paramWan3Refs: Up to {{max}} reference media items, each { "type": "reference_image", "url": "..." }. Wan3 does NOT accept top-level image/images; use this slot only.
video.rejectedWithRefs: Resolutions the upstream rejects when at least one reference image is attached: {{list}}. The form converges to the highest still-legal value automatically.

modelDetail.videoDesc: This is an async task. Submit returns a task id; poll the same path until the status is one of the terminal values, then read the result URL or the failure reason.
modelDetail.imageDesc: The image endpoint is synchronous: the response carries the image URL (or base64) in the data array.

summary.qwenImage30: Qwen 3.0 image generation with Auto sizing, optional references, and prompt-extend / thinking modes.
summary.qwenImage30Pro: Qwen 3.0 Pro image generation with the same parameter contract as the default 3.0 model.
summary.wan27ImagePro: Alibaba Wan 2.7 Pro image generation with 1K/2K/4K discrete tiers and up to 9 reference images.
summary.seedream50Pro: ByteDance Seedream 5.0 Pro image generation with 1K/1.5K/2K tiers, up to 10 reference images, and single-image generation only.
summary.seedream50Lite: ByteDance Seedream 5.0 Lite image generation with 2K/3K/4K tiers, up to 14 reference images, and a 3,686,400 pixel floor.
summary.wan30Video: Alibaba Wan 3.0 text-to-video and image-to-video with 2–30 second durations at 480P / 720P / 1080P and up to 10 reference images.
summary.wan30VideoPrime: High-speed Wan 3.0 sibling with the same request contract as the base model.
summary.minimaxH3: MiniMax H3 video generation with 4–15 second durations at 768P / 2K and up to 5 reference images on Vancine.
summary.seedance20: ByteDance Seedance 2.0 video generation with 4–15 second durations at 480p / 720p / 1080p / 4k and up to 9 reference images.
summary.seedance25: ByteDance Seedance 2.5 video generation with 4–30 second durations at 480p / 720p / 1080p (no 4k) and up to 30 reference images.

description.qwenImage30: Qwen 3.0 is the default Qwen image model. It accepts references (jpeg, png, bmp, tiff, webp, gif) and the same Auto + 4 discrete tier + custom WxH contract as the Pro sibling. agent mode is rejected when references are attached.
description.qwenImage30Pro: Pro sibling of Qwen 3.0. The parameter surface is identical; the difference is upstream quality, not the request contract.
description.wan27ImagePro: Up to 9 reference images (jpeg, png, webp). With any reference attached the upstream caps total pixels at 2048×2048; sending a 4K size with a reference is a 400. The non-Pro Wan 2.7 image model has no published size tier or parameter contract, so it does not appear here.
description.seedream50Pro: Seedream 5.0 Pro only generates a single image per request (n is always 1). Pixel floor 921,600 (1024×1024 works); pixel ceiling 4,624,220. The advanced sequential_image_generation and optimize_prompt_options parameters require PassThrough and are not forwarded by default; this page only documents the wired contract.
description.seedream50Lite: Seedream 5.0 Lite supports 2K, 3K and 4K discrete tiers (pro does not). The 3,686,400 pixel floor rejects 1024×1024 with "image size must be at least 3686400 pixels". Always generates a single image per request. Up to 14 reference images, jpeg/png/webp.
description.wan30Video: Wan 3.0 uses top-level `duration` (integer, seconds) and top-level `size` (one of 480P / 720P / 1080P). Reference images go in `metadata.input.media` as `{ "type": "reference_image", "url": "..." }` — NOT in top-level `image` or `images`. The studio also accepts top-level `seconds` as an alias of `duration`; the upstream rejects top-level `image` / `images` for multi-reference mode.
description.wan30VideoPrime: Prime is the speed-optimised Wan 3.0 sibling. The wire is identical: top-level `duration` + `size`, references in `metadata.input.media`. The only thing the prime variant changes is upstream latency, not the parameter contract.
description.minimaxH3: H3 uses top-level `duration` (integer, seconds) and `metadata.resolution` (exactly `768P` or `2K`). Reference images go in `metadata.content` as `{ "type": "image_url", "role": "reference_image", "image_url": { "url": "..." } }`. Vancine caps reference images at 5 even though MiniMax-H3 itself accepts 9; sending more than 5 is a 400. The `ratio` field is omitted so the plugin applies the documented default.
description.seedance20: Seedance 2.0 uses TOP-LEVEL `seconds` (a STRING — a JSON number is rejected). Resolution goes in `metadata.resolution` (lowercase). Reference images go in `metadata.content` as `{ "type": "image_url", "role": "reference_image", "image_url": { "url": "..." } }`. The upstream rejects `1080p` once a reference image is attached; the studio converges to the highest still-legal value.
description.seedance25: Seedance 2.5 uses top-level `seconds` (a STRING). Resolution goes in `metadata.resolution`. Reference images go in `metadata.content` with `role: "reference_image"`. The supported resolution set is 480p / 720p / 1080p only; the Seedance 2.5 wire has no 4k tier. Maximum duration is 30 seconds; maximum reference images is 30.

ip.model: Must be exactly "{{modelId}}". Model IDs are case-sensitive.
ip.prompt: Free-form text prompt. No fixed character cap beyond the gateway body-size limit; per-model notes live on the model page.
ip.sizeAuto: Auto is the default: the upstream picks the final resolution.
ip.sizeCustom: Custom WIDTHxHEIGHT allowed between {{minPixels}} and {{maxPixels}} pixels, aspect ratio {{minRatio}} to {{maxRatio}}.
ip.sizeCustomWithRefs: With reference images attached the pixel ceiling drops to {{maxPixels}}.
ip.image: Reference image URL or Base64 for image-to-image / multi-image fusion. Up to {{max}} per request. Accepted MIME types: {{mimes}}.
ip.noSeed: Not supported by this model; do not send a seed field.
ip.watermark: Whether to draw a watermark. Default {{default}}.
ip.negativePrompt: Text describing what to avoid. No documented character cap on Qwen 3.x; the gateway body-size cap is the only practical limit.
ip.promptExtendModeAgent: The "agent" mode is rejected when reference images are attached.
ip.enableThinking: Enable thinking mode. Default {{default}}. Requires prompt_extend=true.

qwen30.thinking: enable_thinking is only honored when prompt_extend=true is also set.
qwen30.agentRefs: agent mode is rejected when one or more reference images are attached.

qwen30pro.sameContract: qwen-image-3.0-pro and qwen-image-3.0 share the same public contract; the difference is upstream quality, not the request schema.

wan27pro.refsCeiling: Reference images force a 2048×2048 pixel ceiling; sending a 4K size with a reference image is a 400 from the upstream.

wan27.nonProAbsent: The non-Pro Wan 2.7 image model has no published size tier or parameter contract on the upstream, so it does not appear here.

seedreamPro.singleImage: Seedream 5.0 Pro only generates a single image per request; the upstream rejects n>1.

seedreamLite.pixelFloor: Pixel floor 3,686,400; 1024×1024 is rejected with "image size must be at least 3686400 pixels".
seedreamLite.tiers: Seedream 5.0 Lite supports 2K, 3K and 4K discrete tiers; the Pro model does not.

vp.model: Must be exactly "{{modelId}}". Model IDs are case-sensitive.
vp.prompt: Free-form text prompt. Trimmed before submit; empty is rejected client-side.
vp.durationWan3: Top-level integer, {{min}} to {{max}} seconds. The upstream rejects durations outside this range.
vp.durationH3: Top-level integer, {{min}} to {{max}} seconds. The upstream rejects durations outside this range.
vp.seconds: Top-level STRING, {{min}} to {{max}}. A JSON number is rejected by the gateway (the Go `TaskSubmitReq.Seconds` is a string).
vp.sizeWan3: Top-level resolution: {{list}}. Equivalent to setting metadata.resolution; the studio uses the top-level slot.
vp.resolution: Inside metadata: {{list}}. The Wan3 / H3 / Seedance wire spellings differ; the page above shows the exact string for this model.
vp.refsWan3: Up to {{max}} reference media items, each { "type": "reference_image", "url": "..." }. Wan3 does NOT accept top-level image/images; use this slot only.
vp.refsContent: Up to {{max}} reference image items, each { "type": "image_url", "role": "reference_image", "image_url": { "url": "..." } }. Accepted MIME types: jpeg, png, webp.

wan3.topLevelSlots: Wire contract: top-level `duration` (integer) + `size`; references in `metadata.input.media` as `{ "type": "reference_image", "url": "..." }`.
wan3.noTopLevelImages: Top-level `image` / `images` are NOT accepted: the Wan3 wire rejects them. Multi-reference goes through `metadata.input.media`.

wan3Prime.sameAsWan3: Prime is the speed-optimised Wan3 sibling. The wire contract is identical to Wan3.

h3.slots: Wire contract: top-level `duration` (integer) + `metadata.resolution` (exactly `768P` or `2K`) + `metadata.content` reference items with `role: "reference_image"`.
h3.fiveRefs: Vancine caps H3 reference images at 5 even though MiniMax-H3 itself accepts 9; sending more than 5 is a 400.
h3.ratioOmitted: `ratio` is omitted so the plugin applies the documented default (adaptive for visual input, 16:9 for text-only).

seedance.secondsString: Wire contract: top-level `seconds` is a STRING (a JSON number is rejected by the Go `TaskSubmitReq.Seconds` field).

seedance20.rejectedWithRefs: Seedance 2.0 rejects 1080p once a reference image is attached; the studio converges to the highest still-legal value.
seedance20.tiers: Supported resolutions: 480p / 720p / 1080p / 4k. Maximum duration: 15 seconds. Maximum reference images: 9.

seedance25.no4k: Seedance 2.5 has no 4k tier. Supported resolutions are exactly 480p / 720p / 1080p.
seedance25.limits: Maximum duration: 30 seconds. Maximum reference images: 30. Supported resolutions: 480p / 720p / 1080p.
